correctness.rationale: For d=2p^s, v_p(binomial(d,j)) is at least s-v_p(j). On x=a+pu the linear term divided by p^(s+1) reduces to 2(2a+1)u; j-v_p(j)≥2 for every j≥2, including at p=3. For a≠−1/2 the normalized polynomial is a unit linear map plus p times an integral polynomial, hence a surjective isometry by contraction. Reflection x↦−1−x identifies the two branches in each regular pair, and the reduction 2(x+1/2)^2+1/2 separates all different pairs from each other and the critical class. In the central coordinate x=−1/2+pu, only even powers occur, the quadratic coefficient is exactly A p^(s+2), and the higher coefficients have an extra p after factoring that term. For U integral, the square root g of 1+pU congruent to 1 satisfies (g(u)−g(v))/p=(U(u)−U(v))/(g(u)+g(v)), so u↦ug(u) is identity plus p times a 1-Lipschitz map and is a bijective isometry. At k≤s+1 each pair of classes has 2p^(k−1) inputs and the central class p^(k−1); above that, regular outputs have 2p^s inputs and each central root modulo p^(k−s−2) lifts p^(s+1) times, including at k=s+2. Square-shell counts give Q_p and square-shell measure p/(2(p+1)); the regular and scaled-square measures add to the claimed p^(1−s)/(2(p+1)).
residual_risks: The independent computation is finite corroboration; all p,s,k in scope follow from the coefficient bounds and isometries. No claim for p=2 or arbitrary exponents.

value.rationale: Restricting a modular representation problem to consecutive inputs removes the usual independent-variable sumset structure. The exact two lifting depths identify which targets remain attainable, give their full multiplicities (not just image size modulo p), and quantify how the critical branch contributes to the measure. Uniformity in the ramified exponent and at p=3 makes the classification useful beyond a worked finite example.
residual_risks: The classification is specific to d=2p^s and does not count ordinary integer solutions in bounded intervals.
